metadata.subject: DBMS
metadata.title: Reduce Repeated Data
metadata.description: Diagnose repeated facts and decompose a relation into safer related tables.

learning_objectives: Recognize atomic values and the purpose of 1NF.
Distinguish partial dependencies in 2NF from transitive dependencies in 3NF.
Demonstrate update, insertion, and deletion anomalies.
Construct a dependency-preserving decomposition from declared keys and functional dependencies.

mission.title: Diagnose and normalize a relation
mission.description: Observe repeated facts, identify why they repeat, then split them without losing information.

introduction.title: One fact should have one reliable home
introduction.content: A single wide table can repeat the same student, course, or department fact many times. Normalization uses dependencies to separate facts that belong to different things.
points: 1NF keeps one atomic value in each cell.
2NF removes facts that depend on only part of a composite key.
3NF removes non-key facts that depend on another non-key fact.

worked_example.title: A course name is a course fact
worked_example.content: In ENROLLMENT, the key is student_id + course_id, but course_name depends only on course_id.

steps.explanation: Databases repeats because two students take C10.
course_id alone determines the course name: this is a partial dependency on the composite key.
The course name now has one home while enrollment keeps the relationship.

worked_example.conclusion: The split is not cosmetic: one course-name update now changes one fact instead of several copies.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Use keys, repeated rows, and dependencies to justify each decision.

action_explanations.identify-normal-form: You checked whether each cell contains one atomic value.

quiz.question: A table key is student_id + course_id, but course_name depends only on course_id. What is the core problem?

discovery.title: Normalization discovery
discovery.summary: Normalization follows functional dependencies so each fact has one dependable home, reducing inconsistency and accidental data loss.

sections.title: WHAT?
sections.content: Normalization organizes attributes by what determines them instead of leaving every fact in one wide repeated table.

sections.title: 1NF
sections.content: Each cell holds one atomic value; repeating groups such as a list of phone numbers are separated into individual values.

sections.title: 2NF
sections.content: With a composite key, every non-key fact must depend on the whole key—not only one part.

sections.title: 3NF
sections.content: A non-key fact should not determine another non-key fact. Put that second fact with its true determinant.

sections.title: WHY?
sections.content: Repeated storage creates update inconsistencies, blocks independent inserts, and can erase facts during deletion.

sections.title: REMEMBER
sections.content: Find what determines each fact, then give that fact one reliable home.

alternate_explanations.title: Labelled drawers
alternate_explanations.content: Store each kind of fact in its own labelled drawer and connect drawers with IDs instead of copying the same label everywhere.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow C10
alternate_explanations.content: If C10 always means Databases, store C10 → Databases once in COURSE and let ENROLLMENT reference C10.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how do functional dependencies help prevent update, insertion, or deletion anomalies?
recall.model_answer: Dependencies show which attributes belong together. Separating each fact with its determinant removes repeated copies and protects the fact from inconsistent updates or accidental loss.
